subject: Clarify: prompt storage, backups, and deletion timelines for HIPAA scoping
messages:
From: Lucy Tran <lucy.tran@acmehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: prompt storage, backups, and deletion timelines for HIPAA scoping

Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we're moving toward HIPAA scoping for our pilot, our DPO/legal team needs concise answers on how Redwood handles prompt data, system logs, and backups for regulated workloads. We need this both for our internal DPIA and to populate the SIG/CAIQ rows. Specific asks:

- Do prompts (user-entered text) persist beyond the immediate inference request in Redwood Hosted? If so, where (primary DB, object storage, KV cache, logs)?
- Are prompts included in nightly backups and long-term snapshots? If yes, what is the retention period for those snapshots and the deletion process when a customer requests erasure or at contract termination?
- For encrypted backups, what's the key lifecycle? If an org requests deletion, how do you ensure removal from backups (key rotation, snapshot destruction timeline)?
- Typical timelines we can commit to in an agreement (e.g., deletion from live systems within X days, removal from snapshot rotation within Y days)?

We'd ideally like a one-page summary we can attach to the DPIA and the following artifacts: a sample DPA excerpt we can reference and a CSV with retention windows for logs, prompts, and backups. Can you also flag any SIG/CAIQ rows that may require additional evidence?

Appreciate a short turnaround — do you have answers by COB Pacific today?

Thanks,
Lucy Tran
DPO, AcmeHealth

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Tran <lucy.tran@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: prompt storage, backups, and deletion timelines for HIPAA scoping

Lucy —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a granular breakdown from Neha and Marissa (copied):

- Do prompts persist? Hosted by default: short-lived in RAM/KV cache and logged only for telemetry/quality if the customer opts in; default retention of prompt text is 30 days (configurable).
- Included in backups? Prompts are not written to long-term backups by default. System logs and operational traces are captured and rotated (see table attached).
- Deletion from backups: We operate a snapshot rotation model; deletion requests trigger a live-data purge and start a backup-rotation removal process — see Neha's note for exact windows.
- Commit timelines: Our standard for Hosted is live-data purge within 30 days of request/termination and final removal from backup rotation within 90 days; for Redwood Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate shorter windows (and provide contractual language).

I've attached a DPA excerpt and a quick retention table (redwood-dpa-excerpt.pdf, data-retention-table.csv). Neha, can you confirm the backup key lifecycle and the secure wipe/attestation steps? Marissa, can you add any notes on prompt caching and ephemeral storage for inference?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-dpa-excerpt.pdf (excerpt of DPA: data handling & deletion section)
- data-retention-table.csv (retention windows summary)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Tran <lucy.tran@acmehealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify: prompt storage, backups, and deletion timelines for HIPAA scoping

Hi Lucy — adding operational detail you can include in the DPIA / SIG answers. I kept this high‑level and transportable into questionnaire cells; happy to translate to specific row ids if you send the SIG spreadsheet.

1) Prompt persistence (Hosted):
- Default behavior: prompts are held in-memory and in a short-lived KV cache during the inference session. We retain prompt text for standard telemetry/quality only when customers enable "retain prompts for debugging" in Console. Default retention (when enabled) is 30 days.
- Private/Dedicated: customers can disable prompt retention entirely; for on-prem we run per-customer config and can set 0 days.

2) Logs & operational traces:
- API request/response metadata (non-PII) kept for 90 days.
- Detailed debug traces (may include redacted prompt snippets if enabled) retained for up to 30 days by default.

3) Backups & snapshots:
- Backups: Nightly encrypted snapshots of runtime state (not live KV caches) are kept for 180 days under default Hosted settings. Snapshots are encrypted with customer-segregated keys for Dedicated/Private customers and with service-managed keys for Hosted customers.
- Prompt inclusion: backed-up snapshots do NOT include ephemeral KV cache contents by default. If a customer has enabled long-term prompt retention, those artifacts are stored in object storage buckets and are included in backups — retention in that case follows the bucket lifecycle (default 180 days unless overridden).

4) Deletion / erasure process on request or termination:
- Live purge: We remove live copies from databases/object stores within 30 calendar days of a verified deletion request (or termination effective date).
- Backup rotation removal: We do not perform immediate binary excavation of historical snapshots. Instead, we remove affected artifacts from the next backups (rotation) and ensure they are no longer present in new snapshots; complete removal from snapshot history occurs within the backup retention window (default 180 days). For contractual short windows we offer accelerated snapshot destruction for Dedicated/Private deployments with agreed fees.
- Key-based mitigation: For Hosted customers, when feasible we can leverage key-rotation and crypto-shred of service-managed keys to render older backups unreadable; this is subject to operational constraints and is documented as a mitigation rather than guaranteed immediate deletion.

5) Evidence and attestation:
- We can provide: (a) SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), (b) DPA excerpt (attached), (c) retention matrix CSV (attached), and (d) a deletion attestation letter within 10 business days of a deletion completion for enterprise customers.

6) Suggested contract language (brief):
"Provider will purge customer prompt data from live systems within 30 calendar days of request or termination and will remove data from backup rotation within 180 days, except as otherwise agreed for Dedicated/Private deployments"

If you need explicit SIG/CAIQ row references, send the sheet or row numbers and Marissa and I will populate them.

- Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Neha, Sergio —

Thank you, that is exactly the kind of detail we needed and fits our DPIA template. Two quick follow-ups:

1) Can you convert the suggested contract language into a one-paragraph DPA addendum we can attach to our review packet (DocuSign-ready)?
2) For the timeline you call out, can you confirm you will provide a deletion attestation within 10 business days of final backup removal for our pilot? We need explicit confirmation for our Legal / Audit.

If you can send both items by EOD Pacific tomorrow we can move forward to internal sign-off. Appreciate the quick help — Lucy
